title: Promises and async/await
keyIdeas: A Promise stands for a value that will arrive (or fail) later.
`async` functions always return a Promise; `await` pauses until it settles.
Sequential `await`s run one after another; `Promise.all` runs independent work concurrently.
`Promise.all` rejects as soon as one input rejects.

workedExample.problem: Two independent lookups each take about 50 ms: `getUser(id)` and `getScore(id)`. Write `loadCard(id)` that returns `"Ana: 42"`, loading both concurrently rather than one after the other.
steps: The lookups don't depend on each other, so start both before awaiting either.
Wrap them in `Promise.all([getUser(id), getScore(id)])` and await it once.
Destructure the result array — order matches the input array, not completion time.
Check the timing: concurrent ≈ 50 ms, not ≈ 100 ms.
workedExample.answer: `await loadCard(1)` → `"Ana: 42"` in roughly 50 ms because both lookups run at the same time.

pitfalls: Forgetting `await` (or `return`) and getting a pending `Promise` object instead of the value.
Awaiting independent operations one by one, making the total time the sum instead of the maximum.
Using `Promise.all` when you need every outcome even if some fail — that is `Promise.allSettled`.

citations.quote: A Promise is an object representing the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation.
the then() function returns a new promise, different from the original
Each time when an async function is called, it returns a new Promise which will be resolved with the value returned by the async function
or rejected with an exception uncaught within the async function.
Await expressions make promise-returning functions behave as though they're synchronous by suspending execution until the returned promise is fulfilled or re
If one of the promises in the array rejects, Promise.all() immediately rejects the returned promise.
Promise.allSettled() is another composition tool that ensures all operations are complete before resolving.
These methods all run promises concurrently — a sequence of promises are started simultaneously and do not wait for each other.
